patch.value: GH-1684: pm context TOON focus tables spend 8-10% of the cold-start read on encoding metadata (empty json_columns and absent arrays plus one absent coordinate per unblocked row)

GitHub issue #1684 (reported 2026-11-07 against 2026.11.7 from an agent-UX review). pm context, the canonical cold-start read, prints a <collection>_encoding block under each focus table (high_level_encoding, low_level_encoding) that list and search pages no longer carry after GH-1645 and GH-1674. Reproduced 2026-11-07 on main 70c14d4a3 against this repository's tracker (3,230 items): pm context --limit 5 emits 3,425 B of which 300 B (one block) is encoding metadata; pm context --limit 20 emits 8,510 B of which 629 B (two blocks) is encoding metadata. JSON output has no encoding keys. Where the bytes go: the TOON host (renderToonObjectEntry in src/core/output/output.ts) picks the smallest of expanded TOON, a plain table and a compact table built by encodePmTableRows (src/sdk/output/table-rows.ts). Context focus rows carry blocked and blocker_ids only on blocked rows, so the table needs one absent coordinate per missing cell (14 pairs, about 300 B, at limit 20). The block also names list columns (tags, blocker_ids), all-null columns with their original positions, and empty json_columns and absent arrays. Analysis of the three suggestions in the issue: (1) omitting empty json_columns and absent is lossless only if the decoder treats a missing key as empty; pm-gh1674 deliberately kept them because the table-rows spec decoder, and any host following it, detects an encoding block by both arrays being present, so a change needs a new detection signature (the <collection>_encoding key name the host already reserves) plus a tolerant decodePmTableRows and a migration line. (2) null_columns is not redundant with the header: the header omits those columns because the block declares them, and dropping it loses the explicit-null row facts GH-1500 (pm-4euctr) preserved. (3) list_columns tells a decoder which cells split on the separator; without it a cell like a;b is indistinguishable from a string. So the lossless saving is the empty arrays plus a denser absent encoding, not the null or list declarations. Duplicate check: searched encoding block, null_columns json_columns absent, context TOON envelope; pm-gh1674 and pm-gh1642 (closed) compacted the list and search envelopes only, pm-gh1603 (closed) introduced the compact metadata, pm-sj66lm (closed) owns the get omission receipt, pm-4euctr (closed) owns null row-fact preservation.

pm context TOON focus tables omit empty json_columns and absent arrays and a decoder recognizes the block by its reserved collection_encoding key name; decodePmTableRows restores rows exactly from a block without json_columns or absent, and still decodes every block shape earlier releases emitted; Missing cells use an encoding no larger than the pair list on the pm context corpus, and round-trip tests cover sparse, null, list and nested columns; null_columns and list_columns stay declared so explicit nulls and list cells remain distinguishable, and JSON output is unchanged; A spec measures pm context --limit 20 TOON encoding bytes against the 2026.11.7 baseline and fails on regression, and release notes carry a migration line for TOON table decoders
